s: Which rocket launched the Axiom-4 mission with Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla on 25 June 2025?
x: Axiom-4 was launched aboard a Falcon 9 from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center, Florida; Crew Dragon was the spacecraft.

s: On which date was the Axiom-4 mission, which took Shubhanshu Shukla to the ISS, launched?
x: Axiom-4 launched on 25 June 2025, not 26 June.

s: What was Shubhanshu Shukla’s role in the Axiom-4 mission?
x: Shubhanshu Shukla was the Pilot; Peggy Whitson (USA) was Commander, and the Polish and Hungarian astronauts were Mission Specialists.

s: ISRO’s IADT-1 validated which system of the Gaganyaan crew module?
x: IADT-1 validated the parachute-based deceleration system; it was not an orbital flight.

s: Along with Gaganyaan and the Bharatiya Antariksh Station, which lunar mission is listed among India’s upcoming missions?
x: The upcoming list includes Chandrayaan-4, not Chandrayaan-3.

s: Which of the following Gaganyaan milestone pairs is correctly matched?
x: The crewed flight is targeted for Q1 2027; propulsion systems and the ECLSS engineering model were completed, and TV-D2 was the next test.

s: By which year is the Bharatiya Antariksh Station targeted?
x: The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted for 2035, while the Indian Moon landing is targeted for 2040.

s: Aboard which spacecraft did Rakesh Sharma, the last Indian in space before Shubhanshu Shukla, fly in 1984?
x: Rakesh Sharma flew on Soyuz T-11 in 1984, 40 years before Shukla's Axiom-4 flight.

s: How many ISRO-selected microgravity experiments were conducted on the Axiom-4 mission?
x: India conducted 7 ISRO-selected microgravity experiments; Axiom-4 overall had 60 studies from 31 countries.

s: Who was the Commander of the Axiom-4 mission?
x: Peggy Whitson of the USA commanded Axiom-4; Shubhanshu Shukla was the Pilot.

s: Who became the first Indian to reach the International Space Station?
x: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, on Axiom-4 (2025), became the first Indian on the ISS.

s: From which launch site did the Axiom-4 mission lift off on 25 June 2025?
x: Axiom-4 flew on Falcon 9 from LC-39A, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

s: By which year does India aim to achieve an Indian Moon landing?
x: Targets: crewed Gaganyaan Q1 2027, Bharatiya Antariksh Station 2035, Indian Moon landing 2040.

s: Besides hydrographic survey, what other role does INS Ikshak have?
x: INS Ikshak’s roles are hydrographic survey and HADR / hospital ship.

s: Which of the following statements regarding INS Ikshak is incorrect?
o: It was built by GRSE, Kolkata, with more than 80% indigenous content.
It was the first SVL-class ship with dedicated accommodation for women.
It was commissioned at Kochi by CNS Admiral Dinesh K. Tripathi on 6 November 2025.
x: The incorrect statement is that INS Ikshak means “The Navigator”; its name means “The Guide.” The other statements correctly describe its commissioning, indigenous content and dedicated accommodation for women.

s: INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri were commissioned together on 26 August 2025 at which place?
x: INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri were commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 26 August 2025. Mumbai and Kolkata were the locations of MDL and GRSE respectively, while Chandipur was associated with the IADWS test.

s: Which shipyard built INS Himgiri, commissioned together with INS Udaygiri?
x: Himgiri was built by GRSE, Kolkata, while MDL, Mumbai built Udaygiri.

s: Besides INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri, which group of warships was also commissioned in 2025?
o: INS Surat, INS Vaghsheer, INS Arnala, INS Mormugao
INS Imphal, INS Vaghsheer, INS Arnala, INS Nistar
INS Surat, INS Vaghsheer, INS Arnala, INS Nistar
INS Surat, INS Vikrant, INS Arnala, INS Nistar
x: The other 2025 commissionings were INS Surat, INS Vaghsheer, INS Arnala and INS Nistar; INS Vikrant, INS Mormugao and INS Imphal were commissioned earlier.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Project 17A is incorrect?
o: Project 17A is the follow-on project of Project 17, the Shivalik-class.
Project 17A comprises seven ships, with four assigned to MDL and three to GRSE.
The project has approximately 75% indigenous content and involves more than 200 MSMEs.
Project 17B comprises seven next-generation frigates under Project 17A.
x: The fourth statement is incorrect because Project 17B is the next project involving seven next-generation frigates; it is not described as comprising seven ships under Project 17A. Project 17A is the follow-on of Project 17, has seven ships, and has approximately 75% indigenous content with participation from more than 200 MSMEs.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: INS Udaygiri belongs to the Eastern Naval Command (motto Sanyuktaha Paramojayaha), while INS Himgiri belongs to the Western Naval Command (motto Adrushyam Ajayam).

s: Where was INS Tamal commissioned on 1 July 2025?
x: INS Tamal was commissioned at Kaliningrad, Russia, after being built at the Yantar Shipyard there.

s: Where were MILAN 2026 and the International Fleet Review (February 2026) scheduled to be held?
x: MILAN 2026 and the International Fleet Review were held at Visakhapatnam, home of the Eastern Naval Command (announced for 14-24 February, held 15-25 February 2026). Mumbai hosted the 2001 fleet review.

s: Which of the following statements about INS Tamal is NOT correct?
o: It is the eighth Krivak/Talwar-class frigate from Russia in two decades.
It was the last warship India procured from a foreign source.
It was built at Yantar Shipyard.
It belongs to the Eastern Fleet.
x: INS Tamal belongs to the Western Fleet, the Sword Arm of the Western Naval Command, not the Eastern Fleet.

s: INS Tamal, commissioned in Russia on 1 July 2025, has about what indigenous content?
x: INS Tamal has 26% indigenous content with over 33 Made-in-India systems; about 75% is the Project 17A figure.

s:
Assertion (A): The International Fleet Review is a ceremonial review of ships by the President.
Reason (R): The President is the Supreme Commander.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and the President’s role as Supreme Commander explains the President’s conduct of the ceremonial review of ships. The assertion does not concern MILAN, which is a biennial multilateral naval exercise.

s: Where was India's 2001 fleet review held?
x: The 2001 review was at Mumbai; the 2006, 2016 and 2022 reviews were at Visakhapatnam.

s: What distance does the IASV Triveni circumnavigation expedition, returning to Mumbai by May 2026, cover?
x: The expedition covers 21,600 nautical miles over 8–9 months.

s: Which of the following about IASV Triveni is NOT correct?
o: It began the first-ever tri-service all-women sailing circumnavigation
It was built at Goa Shipyard
It is to return to Mumbai by May 2026
x: IASV Triveni was built at the Indian Naval Dockyard, Puducherry, not at Goa.

s: How many women officers made up the crew of IASV Triveni?
x: The crew had 10 women officers: 5 Army, 1 Navy and 4 Air Force.

s: Under which naval command is MILAN, the biennial multilateral naval exercise, conducted?
x: MILAN is run by the Eastern Naval Command, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, which is why MILAN 2026 is held there.

s: INS Udaygiri, commissioned on 26 August 2025, is named after a mountain range in which State?
x: Udaygiri is named after a mountain range in Andhra Pradesh; Himgiri is named after the Himalayas.

s: INS Udaygiri is which numbered ship designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau?
x: Udaygiri is the 100th ship designed by the Warship Design Bureau.

s: Which was the last Petya-class warship of the Indian Navy, decommissioned at Visakhapatnam in 2003?
x: INS Anjadip, the last Petya-class ship, was decommissioned at Visakhapatnam on 13 December 2003 after 31 years.

s: In which year did the MILAN multilateral naval exercise begin?
x: MILAN began in 1995 and is held every two years under the Eastern Naval Command.

s: Which was the first ship of Project 17A, commissioned in January 2025?
x: INS Nilgiri was the first P-17A frigate (January 2025).

s: Where are two Triput-class frigates being built with Russian design support?
x: Two Triput-class frigates are being built at Goa Shipyard Ltd.

s: Who led the crew of IASV Triveni on the first tri-service all-women sailing circumnavigation?
x: The 10-member crew was led by Lt Col Anuja Varudkar.

s: The Indian Air Force currently has how many fighter squadrons against a sanctioned strength of 42?
x: The IAF has 29 squadrons against 42 sanctioned and needs to add two a year; the AMCA is expected by 2035.

s: What does theaterisation of the Indian Armed Forces refer to?
o: Separate commands for each weapon system
x: Theaterisation means integrating the forces through integrated theatre commands, not separate commands for each weapon system or service.

s: How many MH-60R helicopters has India procured from the US?
x: India procured 24 MH-60R helicopters; 145 is the number of M777 howitzers and 31 of MQ-9B drones.

s: Which pair forms the long-range layer of India’s air defence?
x: Barak-8 and S-400 form the long-range layer, while Akash and MR-SAM form the medium-range layer.

s: Who built the first LCA Tejas Mk1A, due to be handed to the Indian Air Force in October 2025?
x: The first LCA Tejas Mk1A for the Indian Air Force was built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

s: Besides QRSAM and VSHORADS, which of the following is integrated in the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS)?
x: IADWS combines QRSAM, VSHORADS and a high-power-laser Directed Energy Weapon.

s: Under the India–France G2G agreement, Safran will co-develop a jet engine of what thrust for the AMCA?
x: The agreement is to co-develop a 120 kN engine over about 10 years; the AMCA Mk-1 uses the GE-414.

s: Who developed the Centralised Command and Control Centre of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS)?
x: DRDL provided the Command and Control Centre; IADWS is fully indigenous and was not developed with Israel's Rafael.

s: Andhra Pradesh’s Drone City is being established at Orvakal in which district?
x: Drone City is at Orvakal in Kurnool district, over 300 acres.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the 83-aircraft LCA Tejas Mk1A contract is incorrect?
o: Deliveries under the contract were due to begin in February 2024.
Deliveries were delayed because of a shortage of AESA radars.
The delay was linked to the supply of GE Aerospace engines.
x: The incorrect statement attributes the delay to a shortage of AESA radars. The delay was linked to GE Aerospace engine supply; the contract covers 83 Mk1A aircraft, with deliveries due in February 2024 and planned at 1–2 per month.

s: Which of the following is a key upgrade in the LCA Tejas Mk1A?
x: The Tejas Mk1A upgrades include an AESA radar, an electronic warfare suite and better avionics.

s: Which of the following statements about the Project 75(I) contract talks is NOT correct?
o: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd is located in Mumbai.
The talks are between Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd and ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems.
x: Project 75(I) covers six conventional submarines with Air-Independent Propulsion, not nuclear-powered ones.

s: Under Project 75, MDL earlier built which class of submarine with France?
x: MDL built the Scorpene class with France; Types 214 and 218 are TKMS submarines.

s: Which systems form the short-range layer of India's air defence?
x: QRSAM and Spyder form the short-range layer; VSHORADS and MANPADS are the very-short-range layer.

s: The A.P. Drone Corporation, nodal agency for Andhra Pradesh's drone sector, had identified how many use cases?
x: The A.P. Drone Corporation is the nodal agency and had identified 100+ drone use cases.

s: What is the stated objective of the Andhra Pradesh Drone Corporation’s drone-sector initiatives?
o: To establish Andhra Pradesh as the ‘Drone Capital of Asia’
To make Andhra Pradesh the ‘Drone Capital of India’
To make Andhra Pradesh the ‘Space Capital of India’
To develop Andhra Pradesh as the ‘Defence Capital of India’
x: The objective is to make Andhra Pradesh the ‘Drone Capital of India’. The other options alter the stated sector or geographical scope of the objective.

s: In which year did India and the US sign COMCASA?
x: COMCASA was signed in 2018; LEMOA was 2016, BECA 2020 and SOSA 2024.

s: Where is Safran's MRO facility for the Rafale M88 engine, the first M88 hub outside France, located?
x: Safran's M88 engine MRO facility, the first outside France, is located in Hyderabad.

s: Project 75(I), for which MDL began talks with TKMS, involves how many conventional submarines with AIP?
x: Project 75(I) is for six conventional submarines with Air-Independent Propulsion, not nuclear ones.

s: Who is developing AMCA, India's first indigenous fifth-generation stealth fighter?
x: AMCA is by the Aeronautical Development Agency of DRDO; Safran co-develops the 120 kN engine for AMCA Mk-2.

s: Which India-US foundational pact-year pair is correctly matched?
x: LEMOA is from 2016; COMCASA is 2018, BECA 2020 and SOSA 2024.

s: In its maiden flight tests, how many targets did the IADWS destroy simultaneously?
x: IADWS destroyed three targets at once: two fixed-wing UAVs and one multi-copter drone.

s: Which of the following is a 4.5-generation multirole fighter aircraft?
x: Rafale (Dassault, France) is a 4.5-generation twin-engine multirole fighter; MiG-29 is fourth-generation and AMCA will be fifth-generation.

s: Which engine powers AMCA Mk-1?
x: AMCA Mk-1 uses the GE-414 engine of the USA; a 120 kN engine with Safran is for AMCA Mk-2.

s: Where did Rajnath Singh witness the first flight of the LCA Tejas Mk1A on 17 October 2025?
x: The first Tejas Mk1A flight was witnessed at Nashik (HAL).

s: Which systems form the medium-range layer of India's air defence?
x: Long = Barak-8, S-400; medium = Akash, MR-SAM; short = QRSAM, Spyder; very short = VSHORADS, MANPADS.

s: How many MQ-9B drones did India order from the US in October 2024?
x: India ordered 31 MQ-9B drones (~₹28,000 crore) in October 2024.

s: 2026 has been declared the India-France Year of what?
x: 2026 is the India-France Year of Innovation, under the Horizon 2047 roadmap.

s: Which mobile generation was launched during 2009-2012?
x: 4G was launched in 2009-2012; 5G came from 2019 onwards and 6G is expected in 2030+.

s: India accounts for about what share of the world’s chip design engineers?
x: India has about 20% of the world’s chip design engineers; the India Semiconductor Mission was launched in December 2021 under MeitY.

s: Along with the Department of Telecommunications, which body organised India Mobile Congress 2025?
x: The organisers were DoT and COAI, not NASSCOM.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India Mobile Congress 2025 and the 6G vision?
o: IMC 2025 was the 9th edition, held in New Delhi
Data costs in India have fallen by 98% since 2014
The 6G vision projects a $1.2 trillion GDP contribution by 2035
The 6G Symposium was inaugurated by Jyotiraditya Scindia and Narendra Modi
x: The 6G Symposium was inaugurated by Jyotiraditya Scindia and Dr. Neeraj Mittal.

s: The October 2025 AWS outage, caused by a DNS resolution issue for DynamoDB endpoints, originated in which AWS region?
x: The outage, affecting more than 1,000 services, originated in the North Virginia region.

s: In the indigenous 4G stack highlighted at India Mobile Congress 2025, which organisation provided the Core Network?
x: In BSNL's indigenous 4G stack, C-DOT provided the Core Network. Tejas Networks provided the Radio Access Network, and TCS handled integration and data centres.

s: With its indigenous 4G stack, India joined which group of countries that make their own 4G equipment?
o: Denmark, Sweden, South Korea and China
Denmark, Germany, Japan and South Korea
x: India joined Denmark, Sweden, South Korea and China; its stack is described as 5G-ready with export potential.

s: With which organisations did the Bharat 6G Alliance sign MoUs at the 6G Symposium associated with India Mobile Congress 2025?
o: NASSCOM and the European Space Agency
The Department of Telecommunications and COAI
x: The Bharat 6G Alliance signed MoUs with NASSCOM and the European Space Agency. The other options name organisations associated with India Mobile Congress or the indigenous 4G stack, not the MoUs mentioned for the Bharat 6G Alliance.

s: Who developed the 'Made in India' Vikram 32-bit processor shown at Semicon India 2025?
o: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and Semiconductor Laboratory, Chandigarh
U R Rao Satellite Centre and C-DAC, Pune
x: The processor was developed jointly by ISRO's Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Semiconductor Laboratory, Chandigarh; the IITs and NITs showed prototype chips.

s: Which of the following statements about the Vikram 32-bit processor is NOT correct?
o: VIKRAM1601 has been used in ISRO avionics since 2009.
It was developed under the Semicon India Programme.
Its predecessor, VIKRAM1601, was a 16-bit processor.
It builds on ISRO's earlier processor work.
x: The Vikram 32-bit processor was not developed under the Semicon India Programme; it built on ISRO's earlier work, including VIKRAM1601.

s: Which body certified the telecom system powered by domestically manufactured chips?
x: It was certified by the Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), which functions under the Department of Telecommunications.

s: India's semiconductor focus is on mature nodes in which range?
x: India is focusing on mature nodes from 28 nm to 65 nm for automotive, telecom and industrial electronics.

s: What peak speed does the 6G vision target?
x: 6G aims at about 1 Tbps; 10-20 Gbps is the 5G peak and 100 Mbps the 4G mobile peak.

s: In BSNL's indigenous 4G stack, which company provided the Radio Access Network (RAN)?
x: Tejas Networks provided the RAN; C-DOT the core network and TCS the integration.

s: Along with Vikram 3201, which other 32-bit processor came from SCL Chandigarh?
x: Vikram 3201 and Kalpana 3201 are both from SCL Chandigarh.

s: Under which fund is the 100% 4G Saturation Mission run?
x: The 100% 4G Saturation Mission is funded by Digital Bharat Nidhi (~29,000-30,000 villages).

s: Which frequency band is the key technology of 6G?
x: 6G uses terahertz frequencies; mmWave is a 5G technology.

s: Who developed CHACE-2, which recorded the first direct observation of a CME impact on the lunar exosphere?
x: CHACE-2, carried on the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, was developed by ISRO’s Space Physics Laboratory.

s: What happened to the dayside lunar exosphere following the Coronal Mass Ejection observed by Chandrayaan-2’s CHACE-2 payload?
o: Its density rose by more than one order of magnitude
Its density fell by more than one order of magnitude
x: The dayside exosphere density rose by more than one order of magnitude, with sodium, potassium and argon knocked off the regolith. A fall, complete disappearance or no change contradicts the reported observation.

s: LUPEX is a joint lunar mission of India and which country?
x: LUPEX is an India–Japan lunar mission.

s: Where is the Indian Space Situational Awareness and Management Centre (IS4OM) located?
x: IS4OM is in Bengaluru, not Hyderabad.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India’s space security and sustainability measures?
o: India pledged “Debris-Free Space Missions by 2030” at the 2024 IADC meeting it hosted
A ₹27,000 crore programme for about 52 surveillance satellites is planned from 2026
The Indian Space Situational Awareness and Management Centre is in Chennai
The UN COPUOS guidelines referred to are from 2019
x: IS4OM is located in Bengaluru, not Chennai.

s: For which launch vehicle is the second launch complex at Kulasekarapattinam, Tamil Nadu, mainly meant?
x: Kulasekarapattinam is intended for the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV); PSLV and GSLV operations remain at Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh.

s: ISRO’s second launch complex at Kulasekarapattinam will have a capacity of how many launches a year?
x: Its capacity is 20–25 launches a year, with completion scheduled for December 2026.

s: Which of the following space-sector frameworks is wrongly matched?
o: IN-SPACe Norms, Guidelines and Procedures – Authorisation of commercial activities
Catalogue of Indian Standards for Space Industry – Safety
Outer Space Treaty – Province of all mankind and state responsibility for private activities
x: The Indian Space Policy is from 2023.

s: To which institution does CESSI, associated with studying space weather along with Aditya-L1, belong?
x: CESSI is part of IISER Kolkata and is linked with space-weather work.

s: On which date was India's second National Space Day observed?
x: The second National Space Day was on 23 August 2025, marking the Chandrayaan-3 landing.

s: By which year did India pledge 'Debris-Free Space Missions' at the 2024 IADC meet it hosted?
x: India pledged Debris-Free Space Missions by 2030 at the 2024 IADC meet.

s: What is the approximate value of India's programme for about 52 surveillance satellites from 2026?
x: The surveillance-satellite programme is worth about Rs 27,000 crore.

s: In which district of Tamil Nadu is ISRO's second launch complex at Kulasekarapattinam located?
x: Kulasekarapattinam is in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district, Tamil Nadu.

s: Which Article of the Outer Space Treaty (1967) makes a State responsible for the space activities of its private entities?
x: Article VI of the Outer Space Treaty makes the State responsible for private space activities.

s: On which launch vehicle was Chandrayaan-2 launched on 22 July 2019?
x: Chandrayaan-2 was launched on GSLV Mk-III-M1 on 22 July 2019.

s: Which group of countries has comprehensive national space laws, which India still lacks?
x: India has no Space Activities Act; Japan, Luxembourg and the US have national space laws.

s: To which of the following did the ESA–NASA Solar Orbiter study of September 2025 first trace Solar Energetic Electrons?
o: Solar flares and coronal mass ejections
x: Studying more than 300 bursts from 2020 to 2022, Solar Orbiter was the first to trace Solar Energetic Electrons to solar flares and coronal mass ejections.

s: In which year was the ESA-NASA Solar Orbiter launched?
x: Solar Orbiter was launched in February 2020; Parker Solar Probe dates to 2018 and Aditya-L1 to 2023.

s: How long does the Sun's magnetic cycle last?
x: The Sun's magnetic cycle is an 11-year cycle.

s: What was distinctive about the rare quadruple star system UPM J1040−3551 AabBab?
o: Two young red dwarfs were seen orbiting a pair of blue supergiants
Two cold T-type brown dwarfs were seen orbiting a pair of young red dwarfs
A single cold brown dwarf was seen orbiting one young red dwarf
Two blue supergiants were seen orbiting a pair of T-type brown dwarfs
x: UPM J1040−3551 AabBab was the first observed arrangement in which two cold T-type brown dwarfs orbit a pair of young red dwarfs. Blue supergiants are among the hottest and most luminous stars, so they do not fit the system’s description.

s: Red dwarfs, the most common and long-lived stars, make up about what share of the Milky Way's stars?
x: Red dwarfs are the most common stars, making up about 70% of the Milky Way's stars, and are long-lived.

s: Atomic clocks of which element are used in the proposed tabletop experiment to probe the quantum–gravity interface?
x: It uses three entangled ytterbium clocks at different elevations, prepared in a W state robust to particle loss.

s: Which description best applies to the two brown dwarfs in the system UPM J1040−3551 AabBab?
o: They are “failed stars” that cannot sustain hydrogen fusion and may have up to 70 times Jupiter’s mass.
They are the most common stars, forming about 70% of the Milky Way’s stars.
They are among the hottest and most luminous stars in the Galaxy.
They are companions with a chance of occurrence greater than 70%.
x: Brown dwarfs are called “failed stars” because they cannot sustain hydrogen fusion, and their mass can reach up to 70 times that of Jupiter. The 70% figure describes the share of red dwarfs among Milky Way stars, not brown dwarfs.

s: Which quantum gravity theory is associated with extra dimensions and gravitons?
x: String Theory is associated with extra dimensions and gravitons. Loop Quantum Gravity instead describes discrete spacetime at the Planck scale, making it the tempting but incorrect alternative.

s: Which spacecraft was the first to image the Sun's poles?
x: The ESA-NASA Solar Orbiter was the first to image the Sun's poles; Parker Solar Probe made the closest approach.

s: Which spacecraft holds the record for the closest approach to the Sun?
x: NASA's Parker Solar Probe (2018) made the closest approach to the Sun; Solar Orbiter first imaged the poles.

s: Which theory of quantum gravity treats spacetime as discrete at the Planck scale?
x: Loop Quantum Gravity = discrete spacetime; String Theory = extra dimensions and gravitons.

s: Which regiment provided India's contingent for Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2025 at Fort Wainwright, Alaska?
x: India fielded a battalion of the Madras Regiment; the US unit was the 1st Battalion, 5th Infantry Regiment.

s: The Konkan-25 India–UK carrier strike group exercise had which two phases?
x: Konkan-25 consisted of a Sea phase and a Harbour phase.

s: Exercise Konkan, linked with Vision 2035 and the IPOI, is a naval exercise between India and which country?
x: Konkan is an India–UK exercise, associated with India-UK Vision 2035, and is named after the Konkan Coast.

s: Konkan-25 (October 2025) was the first-ever India–UK bilateral exercise involving which of the following of both countries?
x: Konkan-25 was the first-ever bilateral Carrier Strike Group exercise involving both Indian and UK carrier groups.

s: In the Konkan-25 carrier strike group exercise, which aircraft was a UK asset?
x: The F-35B flew from HMS Prince of Wales; MiG-29K, Kamov-31 and LCA-Navy were on INS Vikrant.

s: Which Indian naval vessel reached Alexandria, Egypt, on 1 September 2025 for participation in Exercise Bright Star 2025?
x: INS Trikand, a Talwar-class stealth frigate, reached Alexandria on 1 September 2025 for Exercise Bright Star 2025. INS Shivalik, INS Kolkata and INS Vikrant were not identified as the vessel in this event.

s: Which of the following countries was NOT a participant in Exercise Bright Star 2025?
x: Bright Star 2025 included India, Egypt, the US, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Greece, Cyprus and Italy; France was not listed.

s: Exercise Bright Star originated as a US–Egypt bilateral exercise in which year?
x: Exercise Bright Star originated in 1980 as a US–Egypt bilateral exercise.

s: Which of the following statements about Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2025 is NOT correct?
o: UN peacekeeping was not among its areas of focus.
It included UAS and counter-UAS operations.
It included high-altitude and mountain warfare.
x: UN peacekeeping was among the focus areas of Yudh Abhyas 2025, along with mountain warfare, heliborne and UAS/counter-UAS operations.

s: Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2025 between India and the US was which edition?
x: Yudh Abhyas 2025 at Fort Wainwright, Alaska was the 21st edition; the series began in 2004.

s: When did the Union Cabinet approve the Research Development and Innovation Scheme?
x: The RDI Scheme was approved in July 2025; around 70% of ANRF’s budget is to come from private sources.

s: Which of the following women-in-STEM items is wrongly matched?
o: STEM – Term coined in 2001 by UNESCO
WISE-KIRAN – Career-break re-entry for women scientists aged 27–57
Women in STEMM (WiS) – Scholarships and fellowships
x: The term STEM was coined in 2001 by the US National Science Foundation.

s: Which body issued an advisory against the use of ChatGPT in board examinations?
x: CBSE issued the advisory against ChatGPT in board examinations.

s: Who created the World Wide Web?
x: Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web.

s: By what other name is General AI known?
x: General AI is called strong AI, while narrow AI is called weak AI.

s: In February 2025, how did OpenAI's Sam Altman rank India among OpenAI's markets by users?
x: OpenAI identified India as its second-largest market by users, not the largest.

s: From which class will the Ministry of Education introduce AI in the curriculum from the academic year 2026–27?
x: AI enters the curriculum from Class 3 in 2026–27; CBSE schools already offer AI as a skill subject from Class 6.

s: Which approach was suggested to tackle school constraints while introducing AI in the curriculum from Class 3?
o: Mandatory computer labs in every school
x: Unplugged curricula were suggested for schools facing constraints such as single teachers or fewer than 50 students.

s: Which of the following about AI and news copyright is NOT correct?
o: Fair use requires compensation to be paid to publishers
Large language models have been trained on news content without consent or compensation
In India, DPIIT formed a committee on copyright and AI
Australia and Canada have laws making tech giants pay news publishers
x: Fair use allows limited use without permission and does not require payment.

s: In the context of AI applications in healthcare, what can AI forecast in Kenya up to six months ahead?
x: AI can forecast child malnutrition in Kenya up to six months ahead. Oncology drug discovery is associated with IBM Watson and Exscientia, not the stated forecasting application.

s: Under the Trump administration, what fee was announced for an H-1B visa?
x: The H-1B fee under the Trump administration was $100,000. The other amounts do not match the announced fee.

s: In LLM training, which stage uses human labels?
x: Supervised learning uses human labels; reinforcement learning uses human feedback.

s: Under the proposed MeitY rules, a label on visual AI-generated content must cover at least what share of its surface area?
x: Visual labels must cover at least 10% of the surface area; audio labels the initial 10% of the duration.

s: Who launched SARAL, the AI tool that generates layperson-friendly summaries of research papers?
x: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) launched SARAL, which uses AI and NLP to summarise research papers.

s: What must platforms do under the proposed rules on AI-generated content?
o: Take user declarations only, without verifying them
Verify content only on government request
Take user declarations and verify them
Rely solely on users reporting violations
x: Platforms must take user declarations and verify them, with metadata for traceability.

s: By amplifying what do engagement-driven algorithms mainly contribute to affective polarisation and echo chambers?
x: Such algorithms amplify outrage to drive engagement, feeding polarisation, echo chambers and misinformation.

s: Which two bodies were launched by the United Nations General Assembly in connection with artificial intelligence governance?
o: International Telecommunication Union AI Forum and UN AI Court
Global Digital Compact Council and International AI Safety Board
UN Scientific Panel on Climate Change and Global Digital Dialogue
UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and Global Dialogue on AI Governance
x: The two bodies are the UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and the Global Dialogue on AI Governance. The Global Digital Compact is the framework to which this initiative is linked, not the name of either body.

s: Which countries were cited for laws requiring technology giants to pay news publishers in the context of AI and copyright?
x: Australia and Canada were cited as precedents for laws making technology giants pay publishers. The other country combinations are not the pair identified in this copyright discussion.

s: Under 'fair use' in the AI-and-news copyright debate, how may content be used without permission?
o: Only to a limited extent, with no mandatory compensation
Without any limit and without compensation
Only to a limited extent, with mandatory compensation
x: Fair use permits only limited use without permission and does not mandate compensation.

s: From which class does CBSE already offer AI as a skill subject?
x: CBSE offers AI as a skill subject from Class 6; AI from Class 3 starts in 2026-27.

s: Which of the following about the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance is NOT correct?
o: Its session in Geneva is scheduled for July 2026
A session in New York is scheduled for 2027
It was launched by the UN Security Council
The UN Secretary-General called it a 'pathbreaking milestone'
x: The Global Dialogue on AI Governance was launched by the UN General Assembly (with the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI), not the Security Council. Sessions are in Geneva (July 2026) and New York (2027); Antonio Guterres called it a 'pathbreaking milestone'.

s: Adult neurogenesis in humans has been confirmed in which brain region?
x: New neurons form in the hippocampal dentate gyrus, shown using single-cell RNA sequencing and AI; the cortex and hypothalamus show no consistent adult neurogenesis.

s: The first US human case of New World screwworm, confirmed on 24 August 2025, was in a traveller returning from which country?
x: The case was in a traveller returning from El Salvador.

s: What was Kerala's fatality rate for Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM)?
x: Kerala’s PAM fatality rate was about 25%, against about 97% globally.

s: At which ICMR-Regional Medical Research Centre was AdFalciVax, India's first indigenous multi-stage malaria vaccine, developed?
x: AdFalciVax was developed by ICMR-RMRC Bhubaneswar using Lactococcus lactis, with ICMR-NIMR and NII.

s: Which organisation, for the first time, endorsed GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity?
x: The World Health Organization endorsed GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity for the first time. The World Trade Organization is the tempting alternative, but the endorsement was by the World Health Organization.

s: Mounjaro and Zepbound are brand names of which drug?
x: Tirzepatide is sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound; semaglutide is sold as Ozempic and Wegovy.

s: Dr. Reddy's, Cipla and Biocon are preparing biosimilars of which weight-loss drugs after patent expiry around 2025–26?
x: The firms are preparing GLP-1 biosimilars; reported risks include gastroparesis, pancreatitis and thyroid cancer.

s: Which organism causes Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM), reported in Kerala?
x: PAM is caused by the free-living amoeba Naegleria fowleri.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM)?
o: PAM is communicable from person to person
Naegleria fowleri thrives in warm freshwater and soil, up to 46°C
Infection occurs when water enters the nose and reaches the brain through the olfactory nerve
In 2024, a 14-year-old from Kozhikode became the first Indian to survive PAM
x: PAM is not communicable, and it is not spread by drinking contaminated water.

s: CAR-T therapy uses which of the patient’s own cells, genetically modified to attack cancer?
x: CAR-T uses the patient’s own T-cells, not B-cells.

s: For which of the following is CAR-T therapy NOT yet approved?
x: CAR-T is approved for ALL, Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma and Multiple Myeloma; solid tumours are not yet included.

s: What are the major side effects of CAR-T cell therapy?
x: CAR-T therapy's major side effects are Cytokine Release Syndrome and ICANS (neurotoxicity).

s: Along with IIT Bombay, which institution developed InCART, India's first cost-effective CAR-T platform?
x: InCART was developed by IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre; DBT supports Make-in-India CAR-T.

s: In which year was India's first case of Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM) recorded?
x: India's first PAM case was recorded in 1971; 2016 marks Kerala's first case, reported in Alappuzha.

s: In which year did the United States eradicate the New World screwworm using the Sterile Insect Technique?
x: The US eradicated the New World screwworm in 1966 using the Sterile Insect Technique; Florida later saw an outbreak in 2017.

s: A person with which blood group can receive red cells of any group?
x: AB positive is the universal recipient: it has no anti-A, anti-B or anti-Rh antibodies.

s: Red cells of which blood group can be given to a patient of any group?
x: O negative is the universal red-cell donor because it lacks A, B and Rh(D) antigens.

s: When is a person classed as Rh-negative?
o: Lack both A and B antigens
Carry both A and B antigens
x: Rh-negative means the Rh protein is absent; Rh-positive blood given to such a person can cause sensitisation.

s: Which malaria parasite does AdFalciVax, India's first indigenous multi-stage malaria vaccine, target?
x: AdFalciVax is a recombinant chimeric vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum, acting before the parasite enters the bloodstream.

s: The hypothalamus forms the basal part of which division of the brain?
x: The hypothalamus is the basal part of the diencephalon, which belongs to the forebrain.

s: In July 2025, India gifted two Aarogya Maitri Health Cubes to which country during PM Modi's state visit?
x: During PM Modi's state visit, two Aarogya Maitri Health Cubes were handed over to the Maldives in Male on 25 July 2025.

s: What is the full form of BHISHM, the project under which Aarogya Maitri Health Cubes are made?
o: Bharat Health Initiative for Sahyog, Hita and Maitri
Bharat Health Infrastructure for Swasthya, Hita and Mission
Bharatiya Health Initiative for Sewa, Hita and Mitrata
Bharat Hospital Initiative for Sahyog, Health and Maitri
x: BHISHM stands for Bharat Health Initiative for Sahyog, Hita and Maitri.

s: Using which bacterium was AdFalciVax, India's first indigenous multi-stage malaria vaccine, developed?
x: ICMR-RMRC Bhubaneswar developed AdFalciVax using Lactococcus lactis.

s: Ozempic and Wegovy are brand names of which drug?
x: Semaglutide = Ozempic (diabetes) and Wegovy (weight loss); tirzepatide = Mounjaro, Zepbound.

s: Where was Kerala's first case of Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis reported, in 2016?
x: Kerala's first PAM case was in Alappuzha (2016); India's first case was in 1971.

s: For which trait was the genome-edited rice variety MTU-1010 edited?
x: MTU-1010 targets drought and salt tolerance for saline or alkaline soils; Gn1a editing in Samba Mahsuri gave about 19% yield gain.

s: The Nuclear Energy Mission for Viksit Bharat targets what nuclear capacity by 2047, up from 8.8 GW?
x: The Mission targets 100 GW by 2047 from 8.8 GW.

s: How are gene-edited crops without foreign DNA treated under the DBT guidelines?
x: Gene-edited crops without foreign DNA are not treated as GMOs, with RCGM and GEAC providing oversight.

s: Which is India's only commercial GM crop?
x: Bt cotton is India's only commercial GM crop; genome editing changes an organism's own genes without foreign DNA.

s: At which institute did Kutubuddin Ali Molla's team develop the indigenous TnpB-based mini genome editor?
o: Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
National Institute of Plant Genome Research, New Delhi
x: The TnpB-based mini editor was developed at the Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack; IARI was linked to training and IGI supplied newer tools.

s: Who developed DRR Rice 100 (Kamala)?
x: DRR Rice 100 (Kamala) was developed by ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad; Pusa DST Rice 1 came from ICAR-IARI.

s: Which organisation supplied the newer genome-editing tools GeoCas9 and CasLambda used in agricultural genome-editing work?
x: GeoCas9 and CasLambda were supplied by the Innovative Genomics Institute. The Central Rice Research Institute is associated with the indigenous TnpB-based mini editor, while training was conducted at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute.

s: From which body do transgene-free genome-edited plants, exempt from GM biosafety rules, require certification?
x: Under the March 2022 exemption, such plants need IBSC certification, not GEAC.

s: What is the capacity of the BSMR-200 small modular reactor, intended for captive power?
x: BSMR-200 is a 200 MW reactor for captive power, not 300 MW.

s: After whom are Asgard archaea named?
x: Asgard archaea are named after Norse gods, as in Odin-, Loki- and Thorarchaeota.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: FtsZ is the bacterial division protein that forms the Z-ring, while tubulin is the eukaryotic hallmark.

s: Which of the following statements about the IISc study on Odinarchaeota is NOT correct?
o: OdinFtsZ2 anchors directly to membranes without adaptor proteins.
OdinFtsZ1 forms straight protofilaments and anchors directly to membranes.
Odinarchaeota has two FtsZ genes and a tubulin-like gene.
x: OdinFtsZ2 forms spiral ring-like structures and needs adaptor proteins; it is OdinFtsZ1 that anchors directly to membranes.

s: Where was the 108th Indian Science Congress held?
x: The 108th session, the last one held, was at Nagpur.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 109th Indian Science Congress:
1. It was put on hold after Lovely Professional University withdrew as host.
2. The Department of Science and Technology froze its sponsorship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: LPU withdrew and DST froze sponsorship, accusing ISCA of 'unilateral decisions'.

s: In the IISc study on Asgard archaea, which protein is the hallmark of eukaryotes?
x: Tubulin is the eukaryotic hallmark; FtsZ is the bacterial division protein forming the Z-ring.

s: Which institute developed Pusa DST Rice 1, a genome-edited rice variety?
x: Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed by ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, from Cotton Dora Sannalu (MTU 1010).

s: Which is the parent variety of the genome-edited rice DRR Rice 100 (Kamala)?
x: DRR Rice 100 (Kamala) is from Samba Mahsuri; Pusa DST Rice 1 is from MTU 1010.

s: Which group is regarded as the closest living relatives of eukaryotes?
x: Asgard archaea, named after Norse gods, are the closest living relatives of eukaryotes.

s: NIELIT Amaravati, with an outlay of ₹730.70 crore, is an initiative of which of the following?
x: NIELIT Amaravati is a MeitY initiative costing ₹730.70 crore; its classes begin at ANU, Guntur.

s: 'Sangam Digital Twin' is an initiative of which of the following?
x: Sangam Digital Twin belongs to the Department of Telecommunications, not MeitY.

s: Who launched Digiboxx, which offers 20 GB of free cloud storage?
x: Digiboxx is a NITI Aayog initiative; Sangam Digital Twin is of the Department of Telecommunications.

s: Which company opened the Ananta tech campus in Bengaluru in February 2025?
x: Ananta is Google's tech campus in Bengaluru, opened in February 2025.

s: Which was India's first digital village, adopted by ICICI Bank in 2015 for cashless transactions?
x: Akodara in Sabarkantha district, Gujarat, adopted by ICICI Bank in 2015, is India's first digital village.

s: On which National Highway was the first steel-slag road stretch on a National Highway built with CSIR-CRRI technology?
x: The first steel-slag stretch on a National Highway is on NH-66 (Mumbai-Goa), with CSIR-CRRI technology.

s: In which city was India's first steel-slag road built?
x: India's first steel-slag road was built in Surat; the first on a National Highway is on NH-66.

s: Which State launched the 'Digital Detox' initiative (2024) with AIGDF against gaming and social-media addiction?
x: Karnataka launched the Digital Detox initiative in 2024 with AIGDF to fight gaming and social-media addiction.

s: Proba-3 is associated with which objective?
o: Thermal infrared imaging of terrestrial natural resources
Two-spacecraft formation flying to study the Sun’s corona
x: ESA’s Proba-3 uses two-spacecraft formation flying to study the Sun’s corona.

s: OSIRIS-APEX, in the news, is the renamed continuation of OSIRIS-REx. Which asteroid is it now heading for?
x: OSIRIS-APEX is heading for asteroid Apophis. Bennu is the asteroid from which OSIRIS-REx returned samples in 2023. 2024 YR4 is a separate asteroid in the news. Didymos is not the target of this mission.

s: NASA's OSIRIS-REx returned samples in 2023 from which asteroid?
x: OSIRIS-REx returned Bennu samples in 2023; renamed OSIRIS-APEX, it now heads for Apophis.

s: To which country did the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak of Ituri, DRC, declared a PHEIC by WHO in May 2026, spread?
x: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in Ituri, DRC, spread to Uganda; WHO declared it a PHEIC in May 2026.

s: Which disease was reported in June 2026 in Kozhikode, Kerala, and is associated with bats and pigs as hosts?
x: Nipah was reported in Kozhikode, Kerala, in June 2026; bats and pigs are associated with its transmission ecology.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nipah — bats and pigs associated as hosts
x: The Andes strain of hantavirus is rodent-borne, not mosquito-borne. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: How is the Andes strain of Hantavirus, linked to cruise-ship deaths in May 2026, transmitted?
x: Hantavirus is rodent-borne, not mosquito-borne.

s: What are the Aarogya Maitri Cubes under Project BHISHM?
x: Aarogya Maitri cubes under Project BHISHM are portable field hospitals; HLL Lifecare Limited is the nodal agency for sourcing them. They are not missiles, data repositories or launch platforms.

s: How many genomes does DBT's GenomeIndia project cover?
x: GenomeIndia covers 10,000 genomes from 83 population groups and plans to grow to 1 lakh genomes.

s: Where was the 2nd AIIMS Oncology Conclave 2025 held?
x: The 2nd AIIMS Oncology Conclave 2025 was held at AIIMS Jhajjar, the National Cancer Institute (asked 2024). The other AIIMS campuses were not the venue.

s: DBT's GenomeIndia project has sequenced 10,000 genomes from how many population groups?
x: GenomeIndia covers 10,000 genomes from 83 population groups, with a plan to grow to 1 lakh.

s: HLL Lifecare Limited is the nodal agency for sourcing of which of the following under Project BHISHM?
x: HLL Lifecare Limited is the nodal sourcing agency for the Aarogya Maitri Cubes (portable field hospitals) of Project BHISHM.

s: To which country did India send two BHISHM cubes after its earthquake in July 2026?
x: Two BHISHM (Aarogya Maitri) cubes were sent to Venezuela after its earthquake in July 2026.

s: In which Union Budget was NIMHANS-2 announced?
x: NIMHANS-2 was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.

s: The Samudrayaan mission is intended to take human beings to which depth using the Matsya-6000 submersible?
x: Samudrayaan, under the Deep Ocean Mission, aims to carry humans to a depth of 6,000 metres in the Matsya-6000 submersible.

s: Where is the National Atmospheric Research Laboratory (NARL) of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: NARL is located at Gadanki in Chittoor district.

s: Where was the 11th India International Science Festival held?
x: The 11th India International Science Festival was held at Panchkula in Haryana in December 2025.

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of the four telescope-related projects mentioned in Budget 2026–27?
o: National Large Solar Telescope, National Large Optical-infrared Telescope, Himalayan Chandra Telescope upgrade, COSMOS-2 planetarium
LIGO-India, NISAR, Indian Biological Data Centre, COSMOS-2 planetarium
National Large Solar Telescope, AMCA, Himalayan Chandra Telescope upgrade, NISAR
National Large Optical-infrared Telescope, Kusha, LIGO-India, COSMOS-2 planetarium
x: The four projects are the National Large Solar Telescope, National Large Optical-infrared Telescope, Himalayan Chandra Telescope upgrade and COSMOS-2 planetarium.

s: After whom is the 2-m Himalayan Chandra Telescope at Hanle, Ladakh, named?
x: The telescope, dedicated in August 2001 and run remotely from Hosakote by IIA, is named after S. Chandrasekhar.

s: Which of the following pairs (facility – location) is correctly matched?
o: Indian Biological Data Centre – Hanle, Ladakh
x: LIGO-India is located at Hingoli in Maharashtra, and L&T won the DAE contract to build it.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Indian Science Congress is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: 108th session theme – Science and Technology for Sustainable Development with Women Empowerment
Indian Science Congress Association – founded in 1947
x: ISCA was founded in 1914, not 1947.

s: Where was the 108th session of the Indian Science Congress, the last one held, organised?
x: The 108th session was held at Nagpur in January 2023; the 109th at LPU was put on hold.

s: In which year was the Indian Science Congress Association founded?
x: The ISCA was founded in 1914 and holds the annual Science Congress session.

s: Where is the Indian Biological Data Centre of DBT located?
x: The Indian Biological Data Centre is at RCB, Faridabad; LIGO-India is at Hingoli.

s: Which company won the Department of Atomic Energy contract to build LIGO-India at Hingoli?
x: L&T won the DAE contract to build LIGO-India at Hingoli, Maharashtra.

s: Which institute runs the Himalayan Chandra Telescope at Hanle remotely from Hosakote via satellite?
x: The 2-m Himalayan Chandra Telescope is run remotely from Hosakote by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.

s: Which university was to host the 109th Indian Science Congress, which was put on hold?
x: The 109th session was planned at LPU, Punjab, but was put on hold after LPU pulled out and DST withdrew funding.

s: Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) is a single-dose vaccine against which disease?
x: Ervebo is a single-dose Ebola vaccine, though it is not licensed for the Bundibugyo virus behind the 2026 outbreak.

s: Which body oversees genetic manipulation and biosafety in India's biotechnology regulation?
x: DBT handles genetic manipulation and biosafety; CDSCO (headed by DCGI) grants clinical-trial and marketing approval.

s: From July 2026, Advanced Therapeutic Products such as gene and CAR-T therapies come under the licensing of which authority?
x: An amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945 placed ATPs under the Central Licence Approving Authority; DBT only handles genetic manipulation and biosafety.

s: Which of the following describes monoclonal antibodies?
o: target specific molecules and are used in cancer and autoimmune treatment
replace all vaccines used against viral diseases
increase genetic variation across all population groups
x: Monoclonal antibodies are designed to target specific molecules and are used in treating cancer and autoimmune diseases.

s: Who developed the R78C malaria vaccine, which targets the blood-stage antigens RIPR and CyPRA?
o: Oxford and the Serum Institute of India
Novartis and Medicines for Malaria Venture
x: R78C is from Oxford and the Serum Institute of India; Novartis and MMV made Coartem Baby, the first malaria drug for newborns.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Coartem Baby — First malaria drug for newborns
IndOss — First drug for newborn malaria
x: Coartem Baby is described as the first malaria drug for newborns and is WHO-prequalified. Nafithromycin is a macrolide antibiotic, Qdenga is a dengue vaccine, and IndOss is a bone substitute.

s: NexCAR19 is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: India's first indigenous CAR-T therapy for blood cancer
x: NexCAR19 is India's first indigenous CAR-T therapy for blood cancer and received CDSCO approval in 2023.

s: India was certified polio-free in which year?
x: India was certified polio-free in 2014.

s: BIRSA 101 is significant because it is described as India's first CRISPR-based gene therapy for which condition?
x: BIRSA 101 is India's first CRISPR-based gene therapy and is aimed at sickle cell disease, with a tribal focus.

s: Coartem Baby, WHO-prequalified in May 2026, is the first of which of the following?
x: Coartem Baby, by Novartis and Medicines for Malaria Venture, is the first malaria drug for newborns.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: IndOss (CSIR-NCL) is a bone substitute; Nafithromycin is an antibiotic, Qdenga a dengue vaccine and Covishield a COVID-19 vaccine.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Wegovy (semaglutide) is from Novo Nordisk, with a new use for fatty liver disease; Bristol Myers is associated with nivolumab plus relatlimab for melanoma. Qdenga is Takeda's tetravalent dengue vaccine, Nafithromycin is Wockhardt's drug for resistant pneumonia and IndOss is CSIR-NCL's bone substitute.

s: Which Indian company manufactured Covishield, the COVID-19 vaccine developed by Oxford-AstraZeneca?
x: Covishield was developed by Oxford-AstraZeneca and made in India by the Serum Institute of India.

s: Which country became the first to add a malaria vaccine to its routine child immunisation programme in January 2024?
x: Cameroon, in January 2024, was the first to add the RTS,S malaria vaccine to routine child immunisation.

s: Which therapy, approved by CDSCO in July 2026 for melanoma, is India's first LAG-3 dual immunotherapy?
x: Bristol Myers' nivolumab + relatlimab is India's first LAG-3 dual immunotherapy, for melanoma.

s: For which new use did CDSCO approve Wegovy (semaglutide) of Novo Nordisk in July 2026?
x: In July 2026 CDSCO approved Wegovy for fatty liver disease.

s: Which State banned cotton candy in 2024 because it contained the industrial dye Rhodamine-B?
x: Rhodamine-B is an industrial dye not allowed in food; Tamil Nadu banned cotton candy over it in 2024.

s: Which Indian company makes the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine?
x: R21/Matrix-M is made by the Serum Institute of India.

s: What type of missile is Astra Mk 1, developed by DRDO?
x: Astra Mk 1 is a DRDO-developed beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile; Indonesia was its first export destination.

s:
Assertion (A): LRLACM is a subsonic land-attack cruise missile developed by DRDO.
Reason (R): LRLACM has a range of more than 1,000 km.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true (it also uses the Manik engine and succeeds Nirbhay), but its range does not explain its being a subsonic land-attack cruise missile.

s: How is the Agni-4 missile classified?
x: Agni-4 is a nuclear-capable MRBM with a range of about 4,000 km, not an ICBM.

s: In which year was DRDO formed?
x: DRDO was formed in 1958; its motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam'.

s: Which of the following describes Kusha, which underwent its maiden test in July 2026?
o: Subsonic land-attack cruise missile developed by GTRE
Long-range glide bomb developed by JSR Dynamics and BEL
Long-range surface-to-air missile developed by DRDO
Air-to-surface anti-radiation missile developed by RCI Hyderabad
x: Kusha is a DRDO-developed long-range surface-to-air missile. It is described as India’s answer to, or rival of, systems such as the S-400 and Patriot.

s: India's first Vande Bharat Express ran between which two cities?
x: The first Vande Bharat Express ran on the New Delhi-Varanasi route, a fact asked in 2024-25. New Delhi-Katra, Chennai-Mysuru and Mumbai-Gandhinagar were later Vande Bharat routes, not the first.

s: Which of the following is the first indigenous glide weapon mentioned in the context of the 2026 defence developments?
x: TARA is described as the first indigenous glide weapon, developed through DRDO and the IAF, and it underwent its maiden trial.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Khagantak-243 — JSR Dynamics and BEL — Long-range glide bomb
350-kgf expendable turbojet — GTRE, DRDO — Missiles and UAVs
RudraM-II — Cochin Shipyard — Air-to-surface anti-radiation missile
x: RudraM-II is associated with DRDO’s RCI Hyderabad and the IAF, not Cochin Shipyard. Khagantak-243, the expendable turbojet and Samarthak are correctly matched.

s: Where is the flight-test centre for AMCA located?
x: The AMCA flight-test centre is located at Puttaparthi in Andhra Pradesh. AMCA is a fifth-generation twin-engine stealth fighter associated with ADA and DRDO.

s: What type of weapon is RudraM-II, developed by DRDO's RCI Hyderabad with the IAF?
x: RudraM-II is an anti-radiation missile; Khagantak-243 is a glide bomb and LRLACM a land-attack cruise missile.

s: Which country became the first export customer of DRDO's Astra Mk 1 missile?
x: Astra Mk 1, a beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, had its first export to Indonesia.

s: What is the motto of DRDO?
x: DRDO's motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (the source of strength is science).

s: Which agency designs AMCA, India's fifth-generation twin-engine stealth fighter, along with DRDO?
x: AMCA is a fifth-generation twin-engine stealth fighter being developed by ADA and DRDO.

s: AMCA, whose flight-test centre is at Puttaparthi, is a fighter of which generation?
x: AMCA is India's fifth-generation twin-engine stealth fighter.

s: Which missile is DRDO's LRLACM, a subsonic land-attack cruise missile powered by the Manik engine, meant to replace?
x: LRLACM (range over 1,000 km, Manik engine) replaces the Nirbhay cruise missile.

s: Where is the Vande Bharat Express, designed by RDSO, built?
x: Vande Bharat trains are designed by RDSO and built by ICF Chennai.

s: In the NISAR satellite, which radar system is supplied by NASA?
x: NISAR carries dual radar: NASA supplies the L-band system and ISRO the S-band system.

s: Which of the following are covered by the Earth-observation objectives of NISAR?
x: NISAR observes glaciers, earthquakes, land subsidence and biomass, among other Earth-system features.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gaganyaan mission?
o: It is designed to carry a crew of three
It is to fly to a 400 km orbit for three days
IADT-02 was done ahead of the uncrewed G1 flight
x: ESA, not NASA, will give ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan.

s: From where was NISAR, the $1.5-billion Earth-observation satellite, launched in July 2025?
x: NISAR was launched from Sriharikota on 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16. Japan's H3 rocket is linked to Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX, not NISAR.

s: On which rocket is Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX, the ISRO–JAXA lunar south-pole mission, to be launched?
x: LUPEX is to fly on Japan's H3 rocket (around 2028), not India's LVM3.

s: Which mission is described as India's first Earth-imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit?
x: EOS-05, formerly GISAT-1A, is described as India's first Earth-imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit.

s: TRISHNA is a thermal-infrared satellite mission being jointly developed by which agencies?
o: ESA and China National Space Administration
x: TRISHNA is an ISRO-CNES thermal-infrared satellite mission planned for launch on a PSLV.

s: Mission Drishti of GalaxEye is associated with which of the following?
o: India’s first domestic memory-chip packaging plant
The first private Indian 800 kN methane engine
The world’s first OptoSAR satellite launched on Falcon 9
The first private launch from the Dhanush pad using a 3D-printed engine
x: Mission Drishti, developed by GalaxEye, is associated with the world’s first OptoSAR satellite, launched on Falcon 9.

s:
